title: A row gives its cells widths in proportion to weights
body:
Today `row` puts cells side by side on equal units, and a cell can set `span N` to cover several units. No node sizes its children in proportion to numbers. The sufr pipeline figure in `sufr-figures` draws three strips whose pieces have unequal sizes: buckets by count, partitions by size, and the partitions again as stripes in a group box. Each piece is a box whose `at` and `size` a script worked out.

## Proposal

`row` takes `width W` and `weights N...`. The cells share W in proportion to the weights, in order, and the width in `unit` is ignored. With `weights DATA COL`, the weights come from a column of a data file, one cell per row.

```text
row parts { at 60 300; width 1120; unit 0 24; weights 9 12 13 7 8 14 11 10;
    cells "40" "41" "42" "43" "44" "45" "46" "47"; }
```

## Open

- Whether a `gap` between cells comes out of W.
- Whether a `stack` should take `weights` for its children too.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
notes.text: Provisional choices on 2026-11-23, per the rule in CLAUDE.md: `gap` comes out of `width`, and `stack` takes no weights.
